summary.one_liner: A self-hosted bot that runs a local Claude Code session and streams it live into a Slack or Mattermost thread, where teammates can watch and steer it.
summary.what_it_does: The bot runs on your machine and spawns a Claude Code session in a local working directory when someone mentions it in a channel. Output, tool calls, diffs, and a task list stream into the thread, and people can reply or react with emoji to steer the session. Permission prompts appear as 👍/✅/👎 reactions, with three modes (default, auto, bypass) switchable per session. Sessions can invite teammates, use git worktrees, schedule routines, and watch channels for triggers. Claude gets nine MCP tools for chat actions such as posting files, reading permalinks, reacting, and DMing, each with its own guardrail. It works with a Claude subscription or API key, and an optional account pool rotates between accounts.
use_cases: Pair-program with Claude Code with teammates in a Slack or Mattermost thread
Run coding tasks on a local checkout from chat without a cloud sandbox
Approve or deny AI tool use through emoji reactions in a team channel
Schedule recurring Claude tasks that post to a channel
Keep code on self-hosted infrastructure while using Claude from chat
Isolate AI-made changes on a git branch via worktrees
how_to_run: Mention the bot in a channel, e.g. @claude help me fix the bug in src/auth.ts
notable: Multiplayer sessions: invite teammates, gate uninvited messages behind owner approval, and add Co-Authored-By trailers to commits
Emoji-based permission control with three modes switchable mid-session
Runs on your own machine against local checkouts, MCP servers, and plugins, with Mattermost support for self-hosted chat
Built-in channel memory, scheduled routines, and event watches driven by natural language
Multi-account pool routes new sessions to the account with the most subscription headroom
caveats: You must run the bot yourself on a machine that has the repository
On native Windows, auto-restart requires Git for Windows' bash; otherwise WSL is needed
Voice-note transcription requires configuring ElevenLabs Scribe
keywords: let my team watch ai coding
alternative to claude code in slack
